(Standard over operator) [S3, unofficial][S10].

The claim states that the 'Standard over operator' technique involves uploading volume data as a 3D texture to the GPU and rasterizing polygonal slices parallel to the viewpoint. Source [S3] explicitly describes '3D texture mapping' (popularized by Cabral et al. in 1994) as a technique where the volume is uploaded as a 3D texture and the GPU rasterizes polygonal slices through the volume parallel to the viewpoint. Source [S10] corroborates this by noting that real-time volume rendering tools generally prefer to rely on slices facing the view direction (parallel to the viewpoint) to prevent seeing between slices and improve antialiasing. Both sources confirm the specific technical details mentioned in the claim.
